target_customer: Military and homeland security operators of counter-drone systems, and integrators of radars, cameras and effectors
problem: Counter-UAS deployments mix sensors and effectors from many vendors with no single interface, so operators lack one fused picture and fast engagement recommendations.
business_model: Software licensing of an open, hardware-agnostic operating system for defense customers
product_category: Counter-UAS command and control and sensor fusion software (ParallaxOS)

founders.name: Anshul Ahluwalia
founders.background_notes: Built autonomy for Group 3 and Group 5 aircraft per the YC launch post.

founders.name: Cameron Fiore
founders.background_notes: YC page and launch post differ on whether he worked at both firms.

competitors.name: Picogrid
competitors.what: Makes counter-UAS systems communicate with each other

competitors.name: Anduril Lattice
competitors.what: Command and control platform used for counter-UAS, which Surtr plugs into
competitors.traction_then: Incumbent platform with an autonomous interceptor

competitors.name: AirMatrix and Robin Radar unified stack
competitors.what: Radar plus AI validation on a single screen with countermeasure tracking

competitors.name: MatrixSpace Fusion 360
competitors.what: Multi-sensor counter-UAS fusion of radar, optical and RF

technical_complexity.rationale: Fusing radar, RF, camera and acoustic feeds with threat classification and real-time engagement support is difficult for two engineers; founders bring autonomy experience from Shield AI and Anduril.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with many sensors and ITAR licensing create switching costs, but Lattice and other platforms own the command layer.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know; Anduril's Lattice is the incumbent layer Surtr integrates with.

market_need_then: Drone threats in Ukraine and growing US counter-drone spending drive demand. Field tests of ParallaxOS in Kyiv ran through Ukraine's Test in Ukraine program in May 2026 per YesPress, an aggregator.

branding.name_origin: Named after Surtr, the Norse fire giant fated to set the world ablaze at Ragnarok, per one article (Tectonic Defense).

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and technical, 'single pane of glass'

branding.brand_signature: Norse mythology name with ParallaxOS product name

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive mythic name and a defense-appropriate look, but the name is hard to pronounce and there is no community evidence.

outcome_analysis: The company is active, formed in March 2026 and raised a $4.8M seed in July 2026 led by Allegis Capital within months of its Spring 2026 batch. Founders with Shield AI and Anduril experience and field tests in Ukraine support it, while incumbents control the command layer.
notes: Seed amount confirmed by Dealroom and Seedtable (4.8M) while one headline says $5M and some aggregators call it pre-seed; VCBacked lists only $500K (outdated). Education not found for either founder. Comparison dates for Picogrid and Lattice are the date of the Dealroom article, not founding. No outcome news found.
